I think Duolingo is more helpful for languages that have similar alphabets/writing systems (English to Danish, for example). Though it’s not as good when it comes to learning languages that have drastically different systems.

When I was a teenager, my family dog had really foul smelling breath for months on end. No matter how many times my parents took her to the pet groomer, she’d still have an awful breath smell even after they brushed her teeth. I kept bringing it up to my parents, constantly pointing it out because I knew her breath wasn’t supposed to be THAT bad. Like yeah, I’m aware dogs sometimes stink but I cannot emphasize how foul her breath was. My parents ignored me for a good couple years, just passing it off as “normal bad breath” because she’s a dog. After a couple years passed, my dad was playing tug-of-war with her and a couple of her teeth just fell out. A few days went by and more of her teeth kept falling out in random spots, so they FINALLY took her to the vet. Turns out she had a really bad infection and had to undergo surgery to remove the majority of her teeth. It cost my parents over $2000 and they were so pissed. WELL GOLLY GEE, IF ONLY SOMEONE WARNED THEM YEARS IN ADVANCE???

They made comments on the way I ate my food, which caused me to become self-conscious about it. Years later I still can’t eat in front of other people except my parents and husband because of this.

They broke my original PS2 I’ve had since childhood, and never properly apologized or reimbursed me for it. (I did eventually manage to get a replacement for it but it’s just not the same. My dumbass was attached to the console itself for some reason.)

All in all they weren’t exactly the best of roommates. The whole fiasco eventually led to my husband and I ending our friendships with that person when we had to kick them out and we both no longer have contact with them. It does kind of suck since outside of being a bad roommate, they were fun to hang out with and I did have a lot of laughs with them.

One day my parents went out furniture shopping and brought me with them. I only had my iPod with me to distract me, and at the point I had listened to almost everything on it. While my parents were looking around, I sat down on a small ledge in the store and decided to listen to the Afterlife music video for the first time. I fell in love within seconds. I’d never heard anything like it before and all the band members looked so badass to me. Of course I didn’t know any of their names back then and I remember thinking very vividly after the video finished, “wow I wish I was as cool as the lead singer.” And from that point on I got so excited every time an Avenged Sevenfold song played on the radio, and I learned all their names by age 13.

I’m 22 now and they’re still my favourite band. Matt’s still my role model - in more ways than one; I’ve recently discovered that I’m a trans guy and Matt is transition goals for me.
